This case is directly assigned to District Judge Noel Wise. Judge P. Casey Pitts no longer assigned to the case. (This is a text-only entry generated by the court. There is no document associated with this entry.) Any non-CM/ECF Participants have been served by First Class Mail to the addresses of record listed on the Notice of Electronic Filing (NEF) (kab-adi, COURT STAFF) (Filed on 2/24/2025)

ORDER REASSIGNING CASE.IT IS ORDERED that this case is reassigned to the Honorable Noël Wise in the San Jose Division for all further proceedings.1. All future filings shall bear the initials NW immediately after the case number.2. All case management conference dates are vacated and will be reset by the Court.3. All hearing dates presently scheduled are VACATED. However, existing briefing schedules for motions remain unchanged. Motions must be RENOTICED for hearing before Judge Wise by the moving party for a date consistent with the Court’s law and motion calendar, but the renoticing of the hearing does not affect the prior briefing schedule.4. Deadlines for ADR compliance and discovery cutoffs remain unchanged.5. All pretrial conference and trial dates currently set for after May 27, 2025, and all other deadlines associated with the case, will remain in place unless otherwise ordered.6. All pretrial conference and trial dates scheduled on or before May 27, 2025 are vacated. Other pretrial deadlines (eg., motions in limine, pretrial statements, proposed joint trial exhibits, etc.) will remain in place. The Court will notify the parties when a status conference will be held to schedule a new pretrial conference and trial dates for affected cases.7. Matters currently referred to a Magistrate Judge will remain before that Magistrate Judge absent further notice.8. On or before March 17, 2025, the parties shall file a Joint Case Management Statement (separate statements are appropriate if either party is proceeding without counsel). The statement should not exceed ten pages in length and should address all issues outlines in the Standing Order for All Judges of the Northern District. the approved form for such statements can be accessed here: a. The parties are not required to complete a section if inapplicable. As number 20, the statement shall provide the following information: (i) a list or description of each party; (ii) a summary of all claims, counter-claims, cross-claims, or third party claims and the date the complaint and cross-complaint(s) were filed; and (iii) a brief procedural history of the case (chart format welcomed) including, but not limited to, any ADR proceedings or settlement conferences that have been scheduled or concluded and any appellate proceedings that are pending or concluded. b. If the parties believe that an immediate case management conference is needed, the parties shall explain why and identify the urgent matters that require attention. If there is no immediate need, a case management conference will be scheduled or reset pursuant to Paragraph 2 of this Order as needed. 9. The Joint Case Management Statement will not constitute a motion to extend or modify dates. If emergency relief is needed to modify a deadline, and the deadline is not of the type that can be modified via stipulation of the parties without a court order, the requesting party or parties shall additionally file a motion or stipulation for such relief in compliance with Local Rule 6.IT IS SO ORDERED.Dated: 02/24/2025FOR THE EXECUTIVE COMMITTEEMark B.                                   15                  State Bar, Mr. Shahian must explain why he did not report the sanction.

                                  16              8. A thorough explanation of what steps he has personally taken, and when he took

                                  17                  those steps, to ensure that every lawyer in his firm complies with all rules

                                  18                  (including the rules of professional responsibility, rules of court, and rules of

                                  19                  procedure), laws, standing orders, case specific orders, and deadlines.

                                  20                                                   ***
                                  21          The Court continues the OSC hearing as to Plaintiff and Plaintiff’s counsel to May 6, 2026
                                  22   at 1:30 p.m. Mr. Shahian is required to appear in person. No substitutions or video
                                  23   appearances are permitted.
                                  24          Additionally, given this Order and recent orders by other courts, this Court has concerns
                                  25   about SLP and its lawyers dismissing cases when doing so may not be in the best interest of their
                                  26   clients (including clients who may no longer have a viable case if the statute of limitations has
                                  27   run). Plaintiff’s counsel is therefore ORDERED NOT TO DISMISS THIS CASE until further
                                  28   order of this Court. Plaintiff’s counsel is FURTHER ORDERED not to dismiss nor transfer to

                                   2   2026 hearing, without (1) advance written approval from their client, (2) approval from the

                                   3   applicable court, and (3) after Mr. Shahian personally confirms that both the client (by email and

                                   5          To date, the Court has not received correct and complete versions of the parties’ pretrial
